hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this instance-implicit variable only because q appears in the statement via `modularFunctionFieldBar (1 * q)`. `modularFunctionFieldBar` is an abbrev defined in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean (line 111) under only `variable (N : ℕ)`: `laurentBaseChange (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (modularFunctionFieldFull N)`. It has no NeZero, primality or other condition on N, so the statement elaborates for every q, including q = 0 and q = 1. The proof is `rw [Algebra.smul_def]; rfl`. It uses only the default Algebra structure and coercion of an IntermediateField, where `c • g = algebraMap c * g` and the subtype coercion of a product is the product of the coercions. Nothing depends on q being prime. Writing `omit [Fact q.Prime] in` before the theorem leaves the statement and proof unchanged.
